title: A chart is an argument
alt: A whiteboard sketch showing three nearly identical accuracy values of 95.1, 95.4 and 95.7 drawn as bars on an axis starting at 95.0 so they appear seven times different, beside the same values drawn from zero where the bars are indistinguishable; a line chart with a truncated axis marked as legitimate because a change from a baseline is the point, with the rule that bars encode length and must start at zero while lines encode position and need not; the same ten million points drawn as an unreadable solid scatter blob against a hexbin at 0.66 seconds and a two-dimensional histogram at 1.05 seconds, both showing clear density structure; and a red-green line chart rendered as indistinguishable greys under a colour-blindness simulation beside the fix using different line styles and direct labels.

elements.text: the bars differ 7x.  the numbers differ 0.6%.
same data. Same chart type. Opposite conclusion.
a chart is an ARGUMENT. You cannot opt out of making one - you can only choose whether yours is honest.

elements.label: this one is FINE - the axis is labelled, and the change IS the point

elements.text: bars encode LENGTH -> must start at zero
lines encode POSITION -> they need not
and the colour you cannot see
never colour alone. Pair every colour with a shape, a style or a label - the same rule as pairing red with a cross.
